means: A per-lock timeline of every round, both players, as the vendored Triangle engine replays the recorded inputs: what an animated replay draws. Boards are SIMULATED — the .ttrm holds no board snapshot, so no board here was ever compared with the game cell for cell.
not_eligible_because: one simulator, no second independent implementation of the boards
the replay file records inputs and attacks, never the board

caveat.garbage_holes: Garbage hole columns are the ENGINE's seeded-RNG holes. Where `admission.ok` holds they are consistent with the game's own end-of-round counters, garbage cleared and lines among them, both of which depend on where the holes are; but they are never directly observed, and they are not the `x` carried by the recorded garbage events.
caveat.drop_path: Only where each piece ended is recorded here; any path a viewer draws to it is drawn, not the player's key inputs.
caveat.ending: The ending of each player-round is results.gameoverreason; the engine's own topout is not used. Every round is ticked to replay.frames. engine_knockout records whether the ENGINE's board topped out (lock = index of the first lock it did, else null) and whether that agrees with the game ending the player (gameoverreason topout or garbagesmash). Where agrees is false the simulated board may differ from the real one there.
caveat.admission: admission compares the engine's WHOLE-ROUND pieces, lines, holds, garbage cleared, attack, all clears and T-spin clear kinds with report/facts.json. Agreement confirms totals only and does not lift the quarantine.
caveat.prefix: prefix is the existing verified-prefix gate (verifiedBoundary, frame+amount+row) over the existing oracle run: locks <= verified_to are on boards whose attacks matched the opponent's recorded incoming garbage. after = "no_evidence": the attacks ran out, and later locks are neither confirmed nor refuted; "check_failed": the check failed at lock failed_at; "end": verified to the last lock. unrecorded_sim_attacks counts attacks the engine made after the last one the opponent's replay recorded — the gate stops at the shorter stream, so they sit in the no-evidence tail and are counted rather than hidden.

board.coords: y-UP: row 0 is the bottom row; rows >= visible_rows are the buffer above the field

lock_legend.dframe: engine frames since the previous lock (since frame 0 for the first)
lock_legend.place: where the piece ended: shape * (width * rows) + anchor, the shape indexing shapes[piece] and the anchor the yUp * width + x of its bounding box's bottom-left; an ARRAY of cell indices instead when the piece is clipped at the top of the buffer. On a clearing lock these are the cells before the clear
lock_legend.lines: lines this lock cleared; the rows are every full row after placing, which decodeTimeline finds and checks against this count
lock_legend.garbage: [hole column, rows] per insertion made during this lock, in order, applied BEFORE the piece is placed (see decodeTimeline)
lock_legend.held: 1 if hold was used while this piece was the active one. The piece itself and the hold box are derived from seq and this flag (queueStates)
lock_legend.attack: lines of attack this lock generated, before cancellation
lock_legend.sent: what of it was sent after cancelling incoming garbage

seq_legend: the round's piece sequence from options.seed (shared by both players), long enough for hold + next 5 at every lock; see queueStates
